incidents.title: Scammers use AI to impersonate immigration attorneys to dupe immigrants with fake legal services
incidents.summary:
A South Florida immigration attorney, Angel Leal, who has practiced law for over 30 years, is warning the public about criminals using artificial intelligence to impersonate him and defraud vulnerable immigrants. Scammers have created hundreds of fake videos and social media profiles featuring AI-generated images of Leal offering immigration services he never provided. One fraudulent video offered US residency assistance to undocumented immigrants for $2,200. Leal discovered the scheme when potential clients began calling his office, and he says the problem has escalated dramatically over the past three months. His firm hired an anti-piracy company to combat the fraud, resulting in the removal of nearly 6,500 fake profiles across social media platforms, including 3,500 on TikTok, 2,400 on Facebook, and 544 on Instagram.

The scams typically begin with social media videos directing viewers to contact a phone number through WhatsApp, where fraudsters send fake contracts and payment requests. Other deceptive videos feature false testimonials from supposed clients praising Leal's services. Leal warns consumers to be cautious of anyone requesting payment through Venmo, Zelle, or Cash App, and emphasizes that his office never requests payments over the phone. He has changed his personal phone number and plans to contact local and federal authorities this week to investigate the scams further.

incidents.title: ASIC warns scammers are using AI to spin vast webs of deception
incidents.summary:
# Summary

A fake online article featuring ABC finance presenter Alan Kohler and Reserve Bank governor Michele Bullock was designed to promote Boulder Sparhaven, an unlicensed cryptocurrency trading platform. The fabricated interview depicted them discussing the platform in an increasingly heated exchange that ended with Bullock walking out. This type of scam is becoming more common as artificial intelligence makes fraudulent content more convincing and difficult to detect.

The Australian Securities and Investments Commission reports a significant surge in AI-generated investment scams, removing 19,400 scams last year, up 182 percent. Phishing scams increased 279 percent while fake investment platforms jumped 151 percent. Prime Minister Anthony Albanese, Alan Kohler, and billionaire Gina Rinehart are among the most commonly impersonated Australians. ASIC recommends prospective investors verify Australian Financial Services license numbers through their public registers and warns that polished content and familiar branding do not guarantee legitimacy.

incidents.title: Sleep Staging Is Not Guesswork
incidents.summary:
A lawsuit filed by Clarkson Law Firm in San Francisco alleges that Oura, the smart ring company valued at eleven billion dollars, engaged in false advertising regarding its sleep tracking capabilities. The suit seeks class action status and a jury trial, claiming that Oura's devices, which cost three hundred dollars and up, cannot accurately measure sleep stages despite marketing claims to the contrary. The lawsuit contends that Oura's sensors and algorithms lack the ability to detect the physiological signals necessary for accurate sleep analysis and instead rely on artificial intelligence generated guesses comparable to random chance.

Oura disputed the allegations, stating that its products use multiple physiological signals including heart rate and temperature to estimate sleep stages and that independent peer reviewed studies have validated its accuracy against clinical standards. The company emphasized that while its rings are not medical devices, they have been favorably compared to polysomnography in multiple studies. This is not Oura's first legal challenge, as the company currently faces another class action lawsuit alleging it collected personal information without customer consent over a two year period.

incidents.title: Caught in 4K: The Aurora Files
incidents.summary:
# Summary

Gambit Security's Threat Intelligence team discovered that the Aurora ransomware group, active since April 2026, has developed a Linux variant targeting ESXi virtual environments. Researchers identified exposed infrastructure revealing the group's operations across multiple countries. The ransomware uses ChaCha20 encryption and includes an ESXi mode that kills running virtual machines to access disk files while keeping the hypervisor bootable. Aurora operators deployed a custom tool called esxi_finder.py to scan networks for ESXi hosts and vCenter servers by checking ports 443 and 902.

Between April 8 and May 21, 2026, Aurora operators used Cursor Agent running Claude Sonnet to conduct hands-on exploitation against ten target organizations. The AI agent performed tasks including installing VPN clients, scanning networks, enumerating domain privileges, attempting NTLM relay attacks, and running certificate attacks. Researchers also identified a second Aurora cluster targeting eight organizations across multiple countries, using different tactics including SQL Server exploitation and data exfiltration to self-hosted S3 storage. The investigation provided technical indicators of compromise and details about the group's command infrastructure.

incidents.title: A Pizza Hut franchisee is suing over a forced AI system it says wrecked deliveries
incidents.summary:
A Pizza Hut franchisee filed a lawsuit in Texas on May 6, claiming the company's mandatory adoption of an AI-powered delivery system called Dragontail caused major operational problems and over $100 million in damages. Chaac Pizza Northeast, which operates approximately 111 Pizza Hut locations across the Northeast, alleges that the system gave DoorDash drivers visibility into kitchen operations, causing them to batch orders and wait up to 15 minutes for additional deliveries rather than leaving immediately. This practice resulted in delayed pizzas reaching customers, decreased sales, and lower satisfaction scores.

Before the Dragontail rollout in 2024, Chaac achieved over 90 percent on-time delivery rates and double-digit sales growth. After implementation, the franchisee experienced sharp performance declines, with New York City locations dropping from 10.19 percent year-over-year growth to negative 9.78 percent. Chaac contends Pizza Hut failed to provide adequate training and support and ignored worsening metrics while refusing to modify the system. The lawsuit seeks over $100 million in damages plus attorney fees. Pizza Hut declined to comment beyond saying it would respond through legal channels.

incidents.title: Inside the Fake Celebrity Podcast Scam Fooling Hollywood
incidents.summary:
# Summary

Scammers are impersonating Terry Gross and other NPR personalities to solicit money from potential interview guests. Authors, entertainers and public figures have received highly personalized emails claiming to offer appearances on the radio show "Fresh Air," complete with detailed references to their work and professional-looking booking procedures. The fraudulent messages eventually request payment for production costs, typically around $250. Historian Jennifer Black from Misericordia University became suspicious when the email allegedly came directly from Gross herself rather than a production assistant, and she grew more doubtful after spotting AI-like language patterns before being asked for money.

WHYY, NPR and "Fresh Air" have confirmed they are investigating these fraudulent emails and working with law enforcement. The scam has also targeted other celebrities including comedians Nikki Glaser and Amy Poehler and journalist Katie Couric. Experts note that artificial intelligence has made personalized scams more convincing and affordable than traditional mass fraud attempts. WHYY emphasized it never charges guests for interviews and recommends recipients verify suspicious requests through legitimate contact channels rather than responding to suspicious emails.

incidents.title: Fake US thinktank set up and funded by Israel sought to game AI for propaganda
incidents.summary:
# Summary

Israeli officials and contractors set up a fake American think tank called the Hanover Institute to spread pro-Israel propaganda through artificial intelligence systems. Between August 6 and 14, the site published 124 reports totaling over 560,000 words designed to influence chatbots like ChatGPT and Claude. The reports presented Israel's position on contentious issues including alleged war crimes and genocide claims, framed as neutral academic research with citations from legitimate organizations. The operation was part of a broader campaign financed by tens of millions of dollars from the Israeli government and routed through intermediaries including European advertising company Havas Media.

The campaign represents an attempt to manipulate how AI systems present information about Israel by seeding content into training data repositories. Israeli officials have expressed frustration that these expensive public diplomacy efforts have failed to improve Israel's standing in American public opinion, which has shifted significantly toward Palestinians. Recent polling shows only 36 percent of Americans now sympathize with Israel compared to higher levels previously, with particularly steep declines among younger Americans. Experts warn this scheme demonstrates a new threat where foreign governments and others attempt to poison AI training data in ways users cannot easily verify.

incidents.title: Round Hill is suing Suno and Anthropic for up to $1B apiece. It isn’t looking to settle.
incidents.summary:
Major record labels including Universal Music Group, Sony Music, Warner Music, Capitol Records, and Atlantic Records have filed separate lawsuits against AI music generators Udio and Suno. The labels accuse both companies of scraping thousands of copyrighted songs without permission to train their models and of directly reproducing sections of famous songs in their outputs. The lawsuits argue that the companies have been deliberately vague about their training data and that admitting the truth would reveal willful copyright infringement on a massive scale. The record labels submitted a thumb drive of examples demonstrating how specific prompts can generate music that closely mimics copyrighted works from artists including The Beatles, Frank Sinatra, Michael Jackson, and many others.

The record labels tested both AI generators by using targeted prompts describing decades, genres, and artist characteristics, then comparing the outputs to their copyrighted recordings. They discovered they could repeatedly generate songs that replicated the distinctive melodies, rhythms, and styles of well-known tracks. One example involved a prompt about 1950s rock and roll that produced a song closely resembling Chuck Berry's "Johnny B. Goode," while another prompt about Mariah Carey generated a near-identical version of "All I Want for Christmas Is You." The lawsuits claim both companies previously argued their training on copyrighted material qualified as fair use, setting up major court battles about how generative AI services should operate.

incidents.summary:
Universal Music Group has settled a lawsuit against AI music startup Udio, reaching licensing agreements to resolve disputes over copyrighted music used to train Udio's artificial intelligence system. The case alleged that Udio had used songs like The Temptations' "My Girl" without permission to create similar AI-generated music. Under the new agreement, Udio will launch a platform next year trained exclusively on authorized and licensed music, allowing users to create, customize, and share songs. UMG's leadership stated the settlement reflects their commitment to supporting artists and songwriters while embracing new technologies and business models.

Udio, founded in 2024 by former Google DeepMind employees and backed by investors including will.i.am and Mike Krieger, has not disclosed the financial terms of the settlement. The company reported that millions of people have used its platform since launch. This marks Udio's first licensing agreement with a major music label. Artists participating in the new platform will receive compensation, though specific details remain undisclosed. Additionally, UMG announced a separate partnership with Stability AI to develop music creation tools for artists and producers.

incidents.title: AI Hallucinations in State Farm Insurance Outside Lawyers' Filings
incidents.summary:
Lawyers representing State Farm in a Los Angeles lawsuit have admitted to including artificial intelligence-generated fake cases and citations in their legal filings. The homeowner's legal team discovered nonexistent court cases, fabricated quotes, and false legal holdings in motions submitted by State Farm's defense attorneys. Attorney Jacquelene Robinson acknowledged that seven case citations across eight filings simply did not exist, along with incorrect case titles and quotes. Robinson stated she used an AI tool called Irys, mistakenly believing it was connected to her law firm's legal research subscription and would verify citations automatically.

The lawsuit involves homeowner Fa'alagilagi Meni-Siliga, who is suing State Farm and others over insurance claim delays following a 2020 fire that destroyed her home in Carson. She claims that after a storm caused additional water damage during reconstruction, State Farm's delayed approvals prevented completion of repairs, leading her family to bankruptcy and foreclosure. The case is scheduled for trial in October. This incident reflects a growing trend, as approximately 41 percent of law firms now use generative AI, raising concerns about accuracy in legal documents.

Khawaja outlined Pakistan's current efforts to advance its national artificial intelligence and data governance plans to the Saudi official. She emphasized Pakistan's dedication to creating a robust data ecosystem and supporting the nation's digital economy development. stories.Headline: Roundup: Chinese AI gaining popularity in Kenya for affordability, performance, customization
stories.Summary:
Chinese artificial intelligence models are becoming increasingly popular among Kenyan developers and technology companies due to their affordability, strong performance, and customizable open-source design. According to recent data, Chinese AI models represented roughly half of AI use on OpenRouter, up from less than 25 percent a year prior, and accounted for 19 of the 25 most-downloaded open-source systems on Hugging Face. Kenyan companies are adopting Chinese models like DeepSeek and Qwen for applications including legal technology, business intelligence, and document processing.

Local technology leaders highlight that Chinese models consume fewer computing resources than Western alternatives while delivering comparable or superior performance, making them practical for Kenya's limited GPU supply. The open-weight nature of these models allows developers to customize them for local languages and African-specific needs without building systems from scratch. Companies like JibuDocs and Qhala are already leveraging these models for innovative applications, while experts suggest potential uses in healthcare diagnostics and disaster prevention could serve underserved African communities.

stories.Headline: Ghana: Ai Will Enhance, Not Replace Surveyors - Ghis President
stories.Summary:
Emmanuel K. Cobbold, president of the Ghana Institution of Surveyors, addressed members at the organization's 57th Founder's Day Anniversary Celebration in Accra. He encouraged surveyors to adopt artificial intelligence and emerging technologies rather than viewing them as threats to their profession. Cobbold emphasized that while AI can assist with measurements, data analysis, and interpretation, professional surveying still requires human judgment, local expertise, and ethical responsibility. He warned that surveyors who fail to adapt to technological changes risk becoming obsolete as the profession evolves.

The institution is working to help members upgrade their skills to meet changing technological demands while maintaining professional integrity standards. Sarah Esi Ziddah, the organization's chief executive officer, noted that surveyors have significantly contributed to Ghana's development, including providing geospatial data during a boundary dispute with Côte d'Ivoire and supporting construction of an infectious disease center. The event brought together current and former members to recognize contributions to the profession and strengthen professional connections among the organization's widely dispersed membership.

stories.Headline: Environmental News Network - AI Project Led by UH Aims to Protect Hawaiʻi's Coastal Freshwater
stories.Summary:
The University of Hawaiʻi at Mānoa is launching an artificial intelligence project to forecast threats to coastal freshwater supplies and ecosystems. Associate Professor Jonghyun Lee received a $500,000 grant from the National Science Foundation to lead the initiative, which is part of a broader three-year collaborative effort worth nearly $1 million involving the University of Texas at Austin. The project aims to develop AI applications in geoscience to better understand environmental challenges.

Rising ocean levels, intensified storms, saltwater infiltration of freshwater sources, and coastal ecosystem damage present growing dangers to communities throughout the region. These threats directly endanger drinking water availability, farming operations, infrastructure, and the economic wellbeing of millions of people who depend on coastal areas.

stories.Headline: Oklahoma State University adds new AI, logistics programs for fall semester
stories.Summary:
Oklahoma State University Institute of Technology is launching two new academic programs beginning in fall 2026. The first is a 60-credit-hour online Associate in Applied Science in Logistics and Supply Chain Technology that students can complete in four to five semesters. This program covers warehousing, transportation, inventory management, and data-informed decision-making, preparing graduates for careers as logistics coordinators, distribution center managers, inventory specialists, and supply chain coordinators. The second offering is an Applied Artificial Intelligence option within the existing Bachelor of Technology in Information Technologies program.

The university designed both programs to address workforce demands in Oklahoma and beyond. The logistics program prepares students for industry-recognized credentials that can lead to over 11 million jobs nationwide. The artificial intelligence program goes beyond teaching tool usage, instead focusing on applying AI technologies to solve real organizational problems while considering ethics and governance. OSUIT Provost Dr. Richie Roberts stated that preparing students with skills aligned to industry needs helps build a strong workforce supporting the state's economic growth.

Sessions will cover topics such as content creation, personalization, customer experience, marketing automation, and analytics. stories.Headline: Dyna.Ai Selected as Technology Partner in Hong Kong's GenA.I. Sandbox++
stories.Summary:
Dyna.Ai, a Singapore-based AI company, has been selected as a technology partner in Hong Kong's new GenA.I. Sandbox++ program, marking its second consecutive selection by Hong Kong financial regulators. The sandbox was jointly launched by the Hong Kong Monetary Authority, Securities and Futures Commission, Insurance Authority, and Mandatory Provident Fund Schemes Authority in collaboration with Cyberport. Out of nearly 100 regional proposals, 36 use cases involving 30 financial institutions and 27 technology providers were chosen, including major institutions like Bank of China (Hong Kong) and Manulife (International), alongside technology partners Google, IBM, and Dyna.Ai.

Unlike earlier programs focused on generative AI banking pilots, Sandbox++ expands across banking, insurance, securities, and pension funds to test Agentic AI systems that execute complex tasks under real-time governance. Dyna.Ai will demonstrate how financial institutions can safely delegate workflow execution to autonomous AI agents while maintaining strict oversight and compliance. The company plans to showcase its solutions and governance frameworks at LEAP 2026 in Riyadh later this year.
